threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and 30-day onboarding journey map.

messages.text:
Kicking off the launch of our company-wide hybrid onboarding program for the next intake. Goal is to have a standardized 30-day experience that works for both remote and on-site hires, within the 21-day prep window and the 8-hour training cap in week one.

Scope I am proposing:
- Core 30-day journey map with clear touchpoints and owners (T2, future A1)
- Core company and policy training deck
- Manager toolkit and buddy guidance
- HR admin checklist and tracking process
- Feedback surveys and success metrics (T11)

Before we lock this in, I would like input from both of you on:
1) Anything missing from this scope that is critical for your day-to-day.
2) Top 3 success metrics you think leadership will care about.

Please react in this thread so we can converge on the final scope and objectives today.

From a training side, this scope looks solid to me. For the 30-day journey map in T2, I would like to explicitly include:
- A clear split between mandatory vs optional modules to avoid overload in week one.
- At least one touchpoint with the manager and one with a buddy in the first 5 days.

For success metrics, my first pass:
- Completion rate of mandatory modules by day 7 and day 30.
- New hire satisfaction at day 30.
- Manager perception of new hire readiness at day 30.

Happy to translate these into something we can plug into T11 once we agree on the list.

From the HR admin side, I would like to make sure the scope covers:
- A clear checklist for contracts, payroll, and system access (T5).
- A simple way to track who has completed which modules (T7, future A5), so we are not chasing people manually.

For metrics, could we also track how long it takes to get people fully set up in systems? I am not sure if that fits under T11 or if that is separate, but it would help show the impact of the admin checklist.

Agree with the proposed scope and the additions from both of you. One thing I want to highlight is compliance coverage. We need to ensure the journey map and the core deck include all mandatory labour and policy topics, and that they are clearly marked as mandatory.

For success metrics under T11, I suggest we also include:
- Completion rate of compliance modules by day 7.
- Any critical compliance incidents in the first 90 days for new hires who went through the program.

We can track the second one outside the journey map but still reference it in the evaluation framework.

I like the structure. I just want to check one point: for the 8-hour cap in week one, does that include manager 1:1s and buddy time, or only formal training modules? I am asking because it will affect how we design the journey map in T2.

On metrics, could we also consider tracking how many managers actually use the toolkit once it is ready? Maybe a simple yes or no question in the manager survey later.

Good question on the 8-hour cap. For now, I suggest we count only structured training time (live sessions and self-paced modules) toward the 8 hours. Manager 1:1s and buddy check-ins can sit outside that, as long as they are short and focused.

If anyone sees a risk with that interpretation from a workload perspective, we can flag it to leadership when we present the plan.

On toolkit usage, I like the idea of a simple question in the manager survey. We can bake that into the survey templates later.

Works for me to count only structured training toward the 8 hours. I will design the journey map in T2 so that:
- Week one has no more than 8 hours of structured content.
- Manager and buddy touchpoints are short and spread out.

Once I have a first draft of the 30-day journey map (future A1), I will share it here for review and we can check it against the metrics we are defining in T11.

On the metrics side, for T11, could we define who will actually pull the data and how often? For example, if we want completion rates by day 7 and day 30, I can help pull those from the tracking sheet once A5 is in place, but I would need a clear cadence.

Maybe we can start with a monthly report and adjust later if leadership wants more frequent updates.

Monthly reporting sounds reasonable as a starting point. For T11, I suggest we define:
- Metrics: module completion by day 7 and 30, new hire satisfaction at day 30, manager perception of readiness, compliance module completion by day 7, and manager toolkit usage.
- Reporting cadence: monthly summary for leadership.
- Owners: HR assistant for completion data and HR officer for survey and narrative insights.

If leadership later asks for a different cadence, we can adjust without changing the core framework.

I want to double-check the list of metrics so I do not miss anything when we document T11. Are we including time-to-setup for systems as a formal metric, or just as an internal check for the HR team?

If we include it, we will need a clear definition of when a new hire is considered fully set up.

Given the 21-day deadline and the focus on the hybrid onboarding experience, I suggest we keep time-to-setup as an internal operational measure for now, not a headline metric in T11. We can still track it informally using the admin checklist and the tracking sheet, but we will not present it as a core success metric to leadership in this first phase.

If we see strong improvements, we can always add it later as a formal metric.

To summarize where we landed on scope and metrics so I can align T2 and the later training tasks:

Scope for this project pack:
- 30-day hybrid onboarding journey map (T2, A1).
- Core onboarding training deck.
- Manager toolkit and buddy guidance.
- HR admin checklist and completion tracking process.
- Feedback surveys and success metrics framework (T11).

Core success metrics for T11:
- Completion of mandatory modules by day 7 and 30.
- New hire satisfaction at day 30.
- Manager perception of new hire readiness at day 30.
- Compliance module completion by day 7.
- Manager toolkit usage.

Time-to-setup will be monitored internally via the admin checklist and tracking sheet but not reported as a headline metric in this first phase.

If this matches everyone’s understanding, I will proceed with the first draft of the journey map.

That summary matches my understanding and closes the scope and metrics discussion for this phase.

Next step is to get a concrete view of the 30-day journey map so we can validate it against the constraints and metrics.

Sharing the first draft of the 30-Day Hybrid Onboarding Journey Map now (A1). It is structured as:
- Week 1: company overview, HR policies, code of conduct, IT setup, and short manager and buddy touchpoints, capped at 8 hours of structured training.
- Week 2: role-specific shadowing and optional modules.
- Week 3: deeper dives into tools and processes.
- Week 4: consolidation, feedback, and development planning.

Each touchpoint has an owner (HR, manager, buddy, or new hire) and is tagged as mandatory or optional.

Please review with an eye on:
- Compliance coverage.
- Manager and buddy workload.
- Fit with the metrics we defined in T11.

I went through A1 and from a compliance standpoint it looks good overall. All mandatory labour and policy topics are in week one and clearly marked as mandatory.

Two small suggestions:
- Add a short reminder in week 2 for managers to check that mandatory forms are completed.
- Include a note in the journey map that any updates to policies will trigger a quick review of the relevant modules.

With those tweaks, I am comfortable signing off from a compliance perspective.

From the admin side, A1 helps a lot. I can see where the HR assistant steps fit in. One question: for the tracking sheet (A5 later from T7), should we mirror the structure of the journey map, or just list mandatory items?

If we mirror everything, it might be more work to maintain, but it would give a clearer picture.

Looking at A1 from a manager perspective, the touchpoints seem reasonable. The only thing I am slightly concerned about is the number of optional modules in week 3. Some managers might feel pressure to push all of them.

Could we add a short note in the manager toolkit later to clarify how to prioritize optional modules based on role and workload?

Thanks for the detailed review. I will:
- Add the week 2 reminder for managers to confirm mandatory forms are completed.
- Include a note in A1 that any policy updates will trigger a quick review of the related modules.

On the tracking sheet question from earlier, my suggestion is that A5 focuses on mandatory items only, grouped by week. That should keep it manageable while still giving us the data we need for T11.

I have reviewed the updated A1 and it aligns with our scope, constraints, and the metrics we defined in T11. Manager and buddy touchpoints are balanced, compliance topics are covered, and the 8-hour cap in week one is respected.

Unless there are strong objections, I propose we formally approve this 30-day journey map as our baseline for the pilot.

No objections from my side. With A1 approved, we can now align the core deck, manager toolkit, and surveys to this structure.

I will reference A1 when we work on the communication plan and success metrics summary later so everything stays consistent.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize core training content and facilitator guide for live sessions.

messages.text:
I have uploaded the first draft of the Core Onboarding Training Deck (A2) for T3, aligned with the approved 30-day journey map (A1).

Structure of the deck:
- Company story, mission, and values.
- Overview of business units and how they work together.
- HR policies, labour and internal rules, and code of conduct.
- Summary of the hybrid onboarding journey so new hires see the full 30 days.

I also drafted an outline for the Facilitator Guide (T8, future A6) with timing and interaction ideas, but I have not finalized it yet.

I would like feedback on:
1) Any gaps in content, especially compliance-related.
2) What feels realistic for live session duration and format, given the 8-hour cap in week one and manager availability.

Thanks for sharing A2. I did a first pass focusing on HR policies and code of conduct.

Observations:
- All mandatory topics are present, but a few slides could use clearer wording around reporting channels and confidentiality.
- The section on labour rules is quite dense. We might want to split it into two shorter segments or move some details into a handout.

On duration, my initial thought is a 90-minute live session for the company and policy overview, with breaks and interaction built in. That should fit within the week one cap when combined with self-paced modules.

I went through the company story and values sections in A2. Content looks engaging, but I am wondering if we should add a short piece on how hybrid work expectations show up in day-to-day behaviour.

For the live session format, would it be too much to have two separate sessions in week one: one for company and culture, and one for policies? I am not sure if that would push us over the 8-hour limit when combined with other modules in A1.

Splitting into two live sessions could work, but we need to be careful with the total structured time in week one. Looking at A1, we already have IT setup, manager and buddy touchpoints, and some self-paced modules.

My suggestion is:
- One 90-minute live session covering company story, values, and key policies.
- The more detailed policy explanations move into self-paced content or handouts.

This would keep the live time manageable and still give space for interaction.

From the HR assistant side, A2 looks clear. One thing I would find helpful is a slide that summarizes what new hires need to complete in terms of forms and system steps, and by when. That would reinforce what we have in the admin checklist later.

On the facilitator guide (T8, A6), could we include a short note on how to handle questions that touch on individual payroll or benefits cases? I want to make sure trainers know when to redirect those to the right contact.

Thanks for the detailed review. I will:
- Clarify wording on reporting channels and confidentiality in the policy section.
- Split the labour rules content into a shorter live overview plus a handout for details.

On duration, I like the 90-minute live session proposal. I will adjust the deck and the facilitator guide outline so that the live portion fits into that window, with clear markers for what can be moved to self-paced content.

Good call on the forms and system steps. I will add a summary slide that mirrors the key items from the admin checklist and tracking sheet, without going into individual payroll details.

For the facilitator guide (A6), I will include a section on handling sensitive questions, with guidance to redirect individual payroll or benefits topics to the HR support contacts rather than addressing them in the group.

I agree with the single 90-minute live session approach. It keeps things simple for scheduling and respects the 8-hour cap in week one.

To make sure we do not lose important details, we can:
- Use the live session to highlight key rules and behaviours.
- Provide a follow-up email with links to the detailed policy documents and a short quiz in the self-paced module.

This should also help with measuring understanding later.

I am aligned with the 90-minute live session plus self-paced follow-up. One question: do we want to standardize the format as virtual-first (video call) even for on-site hires, or keep an option for in-person delivery?

This will affect how we write the interaction tips in A6.

Given the hybrid nature of the workforce, I suggest we define the standard format as virtual-first, with an option to run the same session in person when it is practical.

In A6, we can:
- Describe the default as a virtual session with breakout discussions and polls.
- Add a short appendix with tips for in-person delivery, so trainers can adapt without changing the core flow.

I have now updated A2 and completed the Facilitator Guide draft (A6) based on the feedback:
- Live session: 90 minutes, virtual-first, with clear timing and interaction points.
- Detailed labour rules moved to a handout and self-paced quiz.
- Added slide summarizing forms and system steps.
- Added guidance on handling sensitive questions and redirecting individual cases.

Please do a final review focusing on whether the content is accurate and the format is realistic for trainers to deliver consistently.

I reviewed A2 and A6 from the perspective of questions we usually get from new hires. The new summary slide on forms and systems is very helpful.

In the facilitator guide, the section on redirecting individual payroll and benefits questions is clear. I do not see any blockers from my side.

I have rechecked the policy and code of conduct sections in A2 and the corresponding parts of A6. The clarifications on reporting channels and confidentiality look good, and the split between live and self-paced content is clear.

From a compliance and HR policy standpoint, I am comfortable with this version.

I checked the flow and timing in A6. The 90-minute structure with interaction points feels realistic, and the virtual-first guidance is clear. The appendix for in-person delivery is a nice touch.

No concerns from my side on the format.

Given the reviews above, I propose we formally sign off on A2 as the standard core onboarding deck and confirm the standard live session format as:
- One 90-minute virtual-first session per intake.
- Supported by self-paced modules and handouts for deeper policy details.

This will be our baseline for the pilot, and we can refine after we collect feedback.

Confirmed. We are locking in:
- A2 as the standard core onboarding deck for the pilot.
- A 90-minute virtual-first live session format, with an in-person option using the same flow.

I will treat this as the baseline for scheduling and for the pilot run-through, and we can adjust after we see survey results and facilitator feedback.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on manager toolkit, HR admin checklist, and tracking process.

messages.text:
I have posted the draft Manager Onboarding Toolkit and Checklist (A3) for T4. It includes:
- A checklist of manager actions for the first 30 days, aligned with A1.
- Sample 1:1 agendas for week 1, week 2, and week 4.
- A simple 30-day plan template managers can adapt.

I would like to align this with the HR admin checklist (T5, future A4) and the tracking process (T7, A5), so managers see a coherent flow.

Please review A3 and share:
1) Any missing manager actions.
2) How we should connect the toolkit to the admin checklist and tracking sheet without overloading managers.

I reviewed A3 and it is very helpful. For the HR admin checklist in T5, I am drafting A4 with:
- Contracts and personal data collection.
- Payroll and benefits setup.
- System access and equipment.
- Mandatory forms and acknowledgements.

To connect A3 and A4, I suggest we:
- Add a short section in the manager toolkit that explains what HR will handle and what managers need to confirm.
- Include a simple reminder for managers to check that the admin checklist items are completed by the end of week 1.

From an HR officer perspective, A3 looks strong. One thing I would add is a short section on how managers should talk about hybrid work expectations in the first 1:1.

On the connection to the tracking sheet (A5 from T7), I think we should:
- Keep the tracking responsibility with HR for module completion.
- Ask managers only to confirm that they have held the key 1:1s and buddy check-ins, which we can capture in a simple field in A5.

Looking at A3 with a manager lens, I like the sample 1:1 agendas. My only concern is that the checklist might feel long for some managers.

Could we:
- Highlight the top 5 must-do actions in week 1.
- Move some of the nice-to-have items into an optional section, so managers can prioritize based on their context.

From the training side, A3 aligns well with A1. The manager actions line up with the touchpoints in the journey map.

I support the idea of keeping the tracking of module completion with HR via A5. In the facilitator guide, I can also reference A3 so trainers remind managers about their role during the live session.

Good point on the length. I will:
- Mark the top 5 must-do actions for week 1 at the top of the checklist.
- Move some of the lower-impact items into an optional section.

I will also add a short paragraph on hybrid work expectations for the first 1:1, as suggested earlier.

On the tracking process for T7 and A5, I can propose a simple structure:
- One row per new hire.
- Columns for completion of mandatory modules, key 1:1s, and buddy check-ins.
- HR assistant updates module completion based on system data.
- Managers only need to confirm yes or no for the 1:1s and buddy meetings.

Would that be enough for our reporting needs without adding too much admin work?

That structure for A5 sounds good to me. It gives us what we need for completion metrics and manager engagement without being too heavy.

We should also document in T7 that HR assistants own updating module completion, and managers are responsible for confirming the 1:1s and buddy check-ins.

I have now updated A3 with:
- Top 5 must-do actions for week 1.
- Optional section for additional ideas.
- Guidance on hybrid work expectations for the first 1:1.
- A short explanation of how A3 connects to the HR admin checklist (A4) and the tracking sheet (A5).

Please do a quick final review so we can decide whether to approve A3 as is.

The updated A3 looks good to me. The link to A4 and A5 is clear, and the must-do vs optional split should help managers focus.

On my side, I will finalize A4 for T5 using the same structure we discussed and make sure it lines up with the summary slide in the core deck.

I like the updated version of A3. The must-do list is very clear, and the hybrid expectations note will be useful for managers who are new to leading hybrid teams.

No further changes from my side.

From a training perspective, A3 is now well aligned with A1 and the live session content. I can reference the must-do actions in the facilitator guide so managers hear a consistent message.

I am comfortable using this version for the pilot.

Based on the feedback, I propose we formally approve A3 as the manager onboarding toolkit and checklist for the pilot.

For the tracking process in T7 and A5, we will:
- Use one row per new hire.
- Have HR assistants update module completion.
- Have managers confirm completion of key 1:1s and buddy check-ins.

This keeps responsibilities clear and supports our reporting needs.

Aligned. A3 is approved for the pilot, and the tracking process and ownership you described for A5 and T7 work for me.

We can revisit after the pilot if we find that managers or HR assistants are struggling with the process.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in communication plan, FAQ, and rollout timeline for pilot.

messages.text:
I have drafted the Onboarding Communication and FAQ Pack (A8) for T9 and T10, and linked it to the survey templates (A7) and the pilot plan (T12).

A8 currently includes:
- Key messages for managers and new hires about the new hybrid onboarding program.
- Email templates for announcing the program and inviting people to the live session.
- A FAQ section with 22 common questions and answers, based on past queries.

I would like feedback on:
1) Clarity of the messages for managers and new hires.
2) Any missing questions in the FAQ.
3) A realistic pilot start date and cohort size, given our 21-day prep window and the status of A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, and A6.

I reviewed the manager and new hire messages in A8. Overall they are clear and consistent with A1 and A2.

Two suggestions:
- For managers, add a short bullet on what support they will get (toolkit A3, admin checklist A4, and tracking via A5).
- For new hires, include a simple visual or short description of the 30-day journey so they understand the flow at a glance.

On the pilot, from a training capacity standpoint, I can handle a cohort of around 15–20 new hires in the first run, assuming we stick to the 90-minute live session format.

The FAQ section in A8 covers most of the questions we usually get. I would add:
- One question about how long it takes to get full system access.
- One question about who to contact if something is missing on day one.

I can also help keep the FAQ updated after the pilot based on new questions that come up.

Looking at the manager communication in A8, I think it would help to be very explicit about what is changing vs the old onboarding approach.

Maybe we can add a short before and after section:
- Before: ad-hoc onboarding, different by team.
- After: standardized 30-day journey with clear roles and tools.

On pilot timing, I want to make sure we have enough time to brief managers on A3 before the first cohort starts.

I agree with the suggestions so far. For the pilot in T12, considering the 21-day prep window and where we are with A1–A6, I propose:
- Pilot cohort: next intake of around 15–20 new hires.
- Pilot start date: three weeks from now, to give us time to finalize A4, A5, and any tweaks to A8.
- Manager briefing: a short virtual session one week before the pilot start, walking through A3 and the key changes.

We should also make sure the survey links from A7 are included in the communication plan so people know when to expect them.

Thanks for the input. I will update A8 to:
- Highlight the support managers receive (A3, A4, A5).
- Add a simple 30-day overview for new hires.
- Include a before and after section for managers.
- Add FAQ entries on system access timing and who to contact.
- Reference the survey links from A7 and when they will be sent (day 7 and day 30).

On the pilot timing, three weeks from now for the start date sounds realistic to me, assuming we stay on track with A4, A5, and the final tweaks to A8.

With a pilot start three weeks from now, I can:
- Block time for the 90-minute live session for the pilot cohort.
- Join the manager briefing to walk through the training flow and how it connects to A1 and A3.

Please confirm the exact date and approximate cohort size so I can send calendar holds.

From the admin side, a pilot start in three weeks works. I will:
- Finalize A4 and A5 in the next few days.
- Prepare a short internal note for HR assistants so they know how the new process works for the pilot cohort.

In A8, could we also add a line telling new hires that they will receive a checklist from HR on day one, so they know what to expect?

I like the updated direction for A8. One small question: in the manager email template, do we explicitly ask managers to confirm that they have read A3 before the pilot starts, or is that too much?

I am thinking about adoption risk and want to make sure managers do not revert to old habits.

Good point on adoption. I suggest we:
- Add a short call to action in the manager email asking them to review A3 before the briefing.
- During the manager briefing, do a quick poll to confirm they have looked at it and address any questions.

That should reinforce the message without making it feel like a heavy requirement.

I have now incorporated all the feedback into A8:
- Clear key messages for managers and new hires.
- Before and after section for managers.
- Visual 30-day overview for new hires.
- FAQ expanded to 24 questions, including system access and who to contact.
- References to A3, A4, A5, and survey links from A7.

Please confirm if you are comfortable approving A8 as the communication and FAQ pack for the pilot.

The updated A8 looks aligned with the journey map and training content. The visual overview and references to the live session format are clear.

I am comfortable using this version for the pilot communication.

From the FAQ and admin perspective, A8 covers what we need. The new questions on system access and contacts are clear, and the reference to the HR checklist on day one sets expectations well.

No further edits from me.

I am happy with the manager messaging in A8, including the before and after section and the call to action to review A3.

This should help reduce the risk of managers defaulting to the old onboarding approach.

Given the feedback, I propose we:
- Approve A8 as the communication and FAQ pack for the pilot.
- Confirm the pilot cohort as the next intake of approximately 15–20 new hires.
- Set the pilot start date for three weeks from today.
- Schedule the manager briefing one week before the pilot start, and send survey links (A7) at day 7 and day 30 as part of T12.

If everyone agrees, we can treat this as our baseline rollout plan.

Aligned. We are approving A8 for the pilot and locking in:
- Pilot cohort: next intake of around 15–20 new hires.
- Pilot start: three weeks from today.
- Manager briefing: one week before pilot start.
- Survey checkpoints: day 7 and day 30 using A7, as part of T12.

I will document this in the evaluation framework and share a short summary with leadership.
